title: The ladder inward
hookLine: Narada keeps asking one question, sir, is there anything greater than this? and every time, the answer is yes
carry: the self is deeper than name and thought
last: ATMAVIT — KNOWING THE SELF CROSSES SORROW.

lines: ALL YOU KNOW IS ONLY NAME.
cards: Kids discover a game early. Why? Because.
But why? Because of this. But why that?
It drives parents up the wall. And yet it's how you get to the bottom of things: keep asking for the next layer down. Sanatkumara has told Narada that everything he studied is only name.
Narada, to his credit, doesn't argue. He asks the next question. Sir, is there anything greater than name?

teach.h: NAME: HOW WE HOLD THE WORLD.
teach.b: The first rung is name. Revere name as Brahman, Sanatkumara says. As far as name reaches, you'll have freedom there.
A fair start: names are how people hold the world. Is there anything greater than name? Yes, speech.
Speech makes the Vedas known, and earth and sky, right and wrong, true and false.

teach.h: SPEECH: RIGHT AND WRONG MADE KNOWN.
teach.b: Without speech, right and wrong couldn't be made known at all. Greater than speech? Mind.

teach.h: MIND HOLDS BOTH, LIKE A FIST.
teach.b: And here's an image from the hand: as a closed fist holds two small fruits, mind holds both speech and name. When you think, let me learn these verses, then you learn them. Let me do this, then you do it.
Greater than mind? Will, samkalpa, intention. When you intend something, then you think it, then you say it, then you give it a name.
Greater than will? Thought, citta: attention, the awareness that notices before you even intend. And Sanatkumara says something pointed here.
If someone knows a great deal but has no real attention, people say: he's nobody. If someone knows little but is truly attentive, people want to listen. Look at the direction of the climb.
Name, speech, mind, will, thought. Each rung is quieter and more inward, and each holds the one below it.

teach.h: REVERE IT AS BRAHMAN. IS THERE ANYTHING GREATER?
teach.b: And at every step, the same pattern: revere this as Brahman, then ask, is there anything greater? Nothing is thrown away. Each thing is honored, then seen through.

That's a core Hindu teaching about who you are: the self, the atman, is deeper than your name, your words, even your thoughts. Sanatkumara is walking Narada inward, toward the one who's paying attention.

how: Teachers of Vedanta often walk students up Sanatkumara's ladder as a contemplative exercise, moving attention from words to mind to awareness.

o: a joke title your friends give you at school
the family title passed from father to son
the first rung of the ladder: how we hold the world

p: holds speech and name, like a fist

s: he says revere name as Brahman; as far as name reaches, there's freedom. then there's something greater.
mind holds speech and name like a fist holds two small fruits
a person who knows little but is truly attentive is listened to
Sanatkumara says so of citta, thought.

games.q: a friend says, 'i am my thoughts. that's all a person is.' what would Sanatkumara ask next?
o: nothing: thought is the top of the ladder.
is there anything greater than thought? the ladder keeps going inward.
why bother with thoughts at all? they're worthless.
games.why: he honors thought, then asks what's greater. on this ladder the self lies deeper than name, speech, mind, will and thought.

practice: Notice a name in your mind, then the inner voice that says it, then the mind behind the voice, then the intention under the thought, then the plain attention that notices all of it.
Rest at that top rung for as long as you can, and when you slip down, climb again.

wordCard.voice: Name. The first rung of Sanatkumara's ladder; above it, speech, mind, will and thought, each greater than the last.

orig.note: Sanskrit nāma: name. the first rung of Sanatkumara's ladder.

carryVoice: Your line: the self is deeper than name and thought. And at every rung, Narada asks again: is there anything greater? See you tomorrow.
